meta.title_en: Chemotherapy Principles: Cell Cycle, Classes, Toxicity and Supportive Care

content.intro: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide, with approximately 10 million deaths in 2020. The pathophysiology of cancer involves the uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells. The cell cycle plays a crucial role in cancer development, with genetic mutations leading to uncontrolled cell division. Chemotherapy targets rapidly dividing cancer cells, but also affects normal cells, leading to toxicity. Understanding the cell cycle and chemotherapy principles is essential for effective cancer treatment. The epidemiology of cancer is complex, with various risk factors, including genetic predisposition, environmental factors, and lifestyle choices. The incidence of cancer is increasing, with a projected 22 million new cases by 2030.

sections.heading: Cell Cycle and Cancer
sections.text: The cell cycle consists of four phases: G1, S, G2, and M. Cancer cells have altered cell cycle regulation, leading to uncontrolled growth. Chemotherapy targets the S and G2 phases, where cancer cells are most vulnerable. Common chemotherapy agents, such as doxorubicin and paclitaxel, work by inhibiting DNA synthesis and cell division. The ESC 2020 guidelines recommend chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for various types of cancer, including breast, lung, and colon cancer.

sections.heading: Chemotherapy Classes and Mechanisms
sections.text: Chemotherapy agents can be classified into several categories, including alkylating agents, antimetabolites, and anthracyclines. Alkylating agents, such as cyclophosphamide, work by cross-linking DNA strands, while antimetabolites, such as 5-fluorouracil, inhibit DNA synthesis. Anthracyclines, such as doxorubicin, intercalate into DNA, disrupting cell division. The AHA 2019 guidelines recommend the use of anthracyclines in the treatment of breast cancer, with a dose of 60-90 mg/m2.

sections.heading: Toxicity and Supportive Care
sections.text: Chemotherapy toxicity can be severe, with common side effects including nausea, vomiting, and myelosuppression. Supportive care, such as antiemetics and growth factor support, can help mitigate these effects. The NICE 2020 guidelines recommend the use of 5-HT3 antagonists, such as ondansetron, to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. The landmark trial, CALGB 9741, demonstrated the effectiveness of dose-dense chemotherapy in improving outcomes in breast cancer patients.

content.clinical_pearl: The use of chemotherapy in cancer treatment can lead to significant toxicity, with up to 50% of patients experiencing severe side effects. However, with proper supportive care, including antiemetics and growth factor support, the risk of toxicity can be reduced, and treatment outcomes can be improved.

sections.heading: Symptoms and Signs of Cancer
sections.text: Cancer can cause a wide range of symptoms, including pain, weight loss, and fatigue. The symptoms can be non-specific, making diagnosis challenging. A thorough medical history and physical examination are essential for identifying the underlying cause of the symptoms. The NICE 2020 guidelines recommend a comprehensive geriatric assessment for older adults with cancer, including evaluation of cognitive function, nutritional status, and social support.

content.intro: The treatment of cancer involves a combination of surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. The choice of treatment depends on the type and stage of the cancer, as well as the patient's overall health. Surgery is often used to remove the tumor, while radiation therapy can help kill any remaining cancer cells. Chemotherapy can be used to treat cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. The treatment of cancer can be complex, with multiple treatments and procedures required to achieve optimal outcomes.

sections.heading: Surgery in Cancer Treatment
sections.text: Surgery is often used to remove the tumor, and can be curative for early-stage cancer. The type of surgery depends on the location and extent of the tumor, as well as the patient's overall health. The NICE 2020 guidelines recommend the use of minimally invasive surgery for the treatment of breast cancer. The landmark trial, NSABP B-06, demonstrated the effectiveness of lumpectomy in breast cancer patients.

sections.heading: Radiation Therapy in Cancer Treatment
sections.text: Radiation therapy can help kill any remaining cancer cells, and can be used to treat cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. The type and dose of radiation therapy depend on the type and stage of the cancer, as well as the patient's overall health. The AHA 2019 guidelines recommend the use of intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) for the treatment of prostate cancer. The trial, RTOG 9406, demonstrated the effectiveness of radiation therapy in improving outcomes in prostate cancer patients.

sections.heading: Chemotherapy in Cancer Treatment
sections.text: Chemotherapy can be used to treat cancer that has spread to other parts of the body, and can be given before or after surgery. The type and dose of chemotherapy depend on the type and stage of the cancer, as well as the patient's overall health. The ESC 2020 guidelines recommend the use of adjuvant chemotherapy for the treatment of breast cancer. The trial, CALGB 9741, demonstrated the effectiveness of dose-dense chemotherapy in improving outcomes in breast cancer patients.
